recipes.name: Louisiana Shrimp Creole
ingredients_raw: 1 pound medium shrimp - peeled and deveined

steps.text: Melt butter in a 2-quart saucepan over medium heat; stir in onion, green pepper, celery, and garlic. Cook and stir until onion has softened and bell pepper is tender, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Mix in cornstarch. Stir in stewed tomatoes, tomato sauce, water, Worcestershire sauce, chili powder, Cajun seasoning, and hot pepper sauce. Bring to a boil, stirring frequently.
Stir in shrimp, lemon juice, and fresh thyme; cook until shrimp are bright pink on the outside and the meat is opaque, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Louisiana Shrimp Creole
raw_recipe.description: In this tasty shrimp Creole recipe, shrimp are simmered in a tomato and green bell pepper sauce. Add as much chili and hot sauce as you can handle!

video.description: In this video, Nicole shows you how to make one of the Gulf Coast’s finest dishes, Louisiana shrimp creole. Using what she calls the holy trinity of veggies, add chopped celery, onion, and bell pepper to a buttered pan and cook them until they’ve softened. Combine the softened vegetables with stewed tomatoes, hot sauce, and a collection of tangy spices to make the thick and rich sauce. With the addition of fresh shrimp, this flavorful and balanced meal is the ideal seafood dinner!

review.reviewBody: This was a great "base" recipes for shrimp creole. As one user stated, the sauce just tasted like tomatoes. I used a 28oz can of crushed tomatoes and tomatoe paste for the sauce. I also had to add aaaaaalot of seasoning to the sauce to give it some flavor. I added paprika, extra worsteshire, red pepper flakes, seasoning salt and a healthy amount of old bay. I added these ingredients a little at a time unti the creole was very flavorful and spicy. Also, after peeling the shrimp I added a little salt and pepper and let them marinate in the fridge with hot sauce for about 20 minutes. Overall, this recipe was great, however if you like your food flavorful you'll need to add a lot of seasonings.
Added 1/3C. chopped parsley, 2 tbl. cajun spice and 2 bay leaves. Increased simmer time by 90 minutes. The base recipe is very good as is.

It gets 3 stars as is. To improve it I substituted 2Tbl of flour for the cornstarch, upped the chili powder to 1Tbl and added 1Tbl of Cajun seasoning (I use Emril's). I also seasoned the shrimp with 1tsp of Cajun seasoning. I left the hot sauce out and added it after cooking for those who don't like the heat I do. Got good flavor with a slight kick of spice before the hot sauce was added. Make it as hot as you want.

Yum! My family really enjoyed this dish. I made some minor adjustments just to accommodate what I had on hand. I used 2lbs of Jumbo shrimp which I peeled and tossed with salt, pepper, and harissa spice and put in the fridge in the morning to sit all day. I doubled the chopped veggies too (more or less) and sautéed them in a roasted red pepper infused olive oil and butter combination. 2T cornstarch was just fine to thicken the stewed tomatoes and tomato sauce (used a 12oz can). I used harissa again in lieu of chili powder and put in some generous glugs of both Worcestershire and a blueberry ghost pepper hot sauce. Thanks for the great recipe!

This was simple to make, and by using only 1 Tablespoon of cornstarch, was the right consistency. I used diced tomatoes instead of stewed. Note to chop the celery small so it softens instead of being crunchy. Didn't use the chili powder and hot sauce since not everyone likes it spicy. Added in crabmeat and served over rice.
The recipe was easy, I simmered the sauce for 2 hours prior to added a combination of shrimp and catfish pieces. Tchin tchin !

I've tried most of the recipes for this dish and this one was the best. Like others I backed off the cornstarch. My only modification was to add a half can of tomato soup and an extra 1/2 lb of shrimp. The tomato soup gave the sauce a slightly sweeter taste which is my preference for this dish. 

One thing that I suggest when cooking your rice is to saute and boil the leftover shrimp shells to make a shrimp stock which I used in place of plain water to prepare my rice. The whole dish was marvelous.

this is a good, easy recipe and it contains what we old cajuns call the "holy trinity", celery, bell peppers and onions. if you can, only buy shrimp exactly the way they came out of the sea, put the shells and heads in 2 cups of water and boil down until you get about 1/8 of a cup and add it to the mixture, it will add much more shrimp flavor, also, folks outside of the area continue to believe that everything we eat is "hot", when we say "spicy" we mean that our food uses many types of spices, not just chili powder or hot sauce

To make this taste more "creole", I only use San Marzino canned tomatoes and "cut" in the spices (use 2 tablespoon of Chile Powder), 3-4 tblspoon of Worcestershire sauce, and double the onions and green pepper. I also used 1.5 lbs of small precooked shrimp instead of medium. Mince the garlic and I used 3 cloves. Hot sauce to taste.

I pretty much followed the recipe as written. I did all the prep work in advance - coarse chopped the veggies, cooked the rice, peeled the defrosted shrimp, and made a little stock from the shrimp peels. Cooking was a snap, although I did extra spices (Old Bay and smoked paprika) as recommended in other reviews. Because we like our sauce more "runny," I added a little "shrimp stock" for the consistency we desire. Just heated up the rice in the microwave and spooned the creole over it. It was delicious and I think can be dish for company!

I tried this recipe last night, and it was very good. After reading some reviews before I made it, I changed it up just a bit. I doubled the onion, green bell peppers, and celery. I used 1 stick of butter and 1/4 flour for the roux, and doubled the tomato's. I added cajun seasoning, in place of the chili powder and 2 lbs of shrimp. It was fantastic!
I could taste the Worcestershire sauce. I'll just cut back a bit for the next time.

Made this exactly as the recipe states except for the thyme. I didn't have any fresh thyme so I used 1 teaspoon of dried thyme. I also didn't use any lemon juice. This was really good and especially for a weeknight meal. It's easy to make and doesn't take long at all. We will definitely have this again. Thanks much for the recipe!
So easy to make! I believe this is my "go to" from now on. Really tasty!
Excellent and easy! I was out of celery and substituted with fennel but it still worked. Also instead of Worcestershire sauce, I used liquid smoke to amp it up. Delicious!
Not bad. Lots of creole recipes out there so this one has some tough competition

Spicier than the shrimp creole I've had in the past, even with only 1 tsp Cajun seasoning. Highly recommend blending corn starch with water before adding to prevent lumps. Very similar to Chef John's Eouteffe but also very tasty!

My husband and I loved this recipe! We followed the recipe except we added a 2 to 3 tsp? sugar, we didn't measure, to balance the acidity some. It was served over some fresh hot Jasmine rice. It's a keeper. It will be made many times in our household. Next time we might try making a roux to get that depth of flavor. Not that it really needs it, but it could only make it better. Thank you for the recipe!
